result.topic_en: Formula-only scratch calculations on second-order partial differential operators in variables alpha and beta (coefficients p, q), transformations of the heat-conduction equation, exponential solutions, and conditions involving logarithmic derivatives of mixed second derivatives.
result.transcription:
$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2}+p\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$ \quad $\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\alpha^2\partial\beta}+p\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta^2}+\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$
$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}+q\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$ \quad $\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\beta^2\partial\alpha}+q\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\alpha^2\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$
$\partial_\beta^2+q\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta$
$\partial_\alpha^2+p\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta$
$2\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}\partial_\alpha^2\partial_\beta+p\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}\partial_\alpha\partial_\beta^2$
$+\frac{\partial q}{\partial\beta}$ \quad $-2\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}$
$-q\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}$ \quad $-q\frac{\partial p}{\partial\alpha}$
$\frac{q\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}-\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}}{1-pq}=\frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}}{\partial\beta}$
$\frac{p\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}-\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}}{1-pq}=\frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}}{\partial\alpha}$
$p e^{\mu t}+\alpha e^{\nu t}+\beta e^{\varsigma t}$
[-$\frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial\alpha^2}+\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}$-]
$\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial z^2}=\mu\alpha$
$\frac{\partial^2\beta}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2\beta}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2\beta}{\partial z^2}=\nu\beta$
$\frac{\partial^2(\alpha\beta)}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2(\alpha\beta)}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2(\alpha\beta)}{\partial z^2}=\lambda(\alpha\beta)$
$p\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2}+q\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+r\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}=0$
$s\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}+\alpha\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}+\beta\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
$+t\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$

$2\frac{\partial s}{\partial\alpha}\partial_\beta^2\partial_\alpha+2\frac{\partial t}{\partial\alpha}\partial_\alpha^2\partial_\beta+q\frac{\partial t}{\partial\beta}\partial_\beta^3$
$+q\frac{\partial s}{\partial\beta}$ \quad $+q\frac{\partial t}{\partial\beta}$
$+q\frac{\partial t}{\partial\alpha}$
$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2}+a\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+b\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}$
$u=b p+b_1 p_1+b_2 p_2+b_3 p_3+\alpha e^{\mu t}+\beta e^{\nu t}$
$\frac{\partial t^2}{\partial\beta^2}$ [-$b_1+\frac{\partial b}{\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial^2 b}{\partial\beta^2}r+\frac{\partial^2 b}{\partial\beta^2}s$-]
[-$\frac{\partial t}{\partial\alpha}$-]
$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+a\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}+b\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}$
$p\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\alpha^3}+q\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2}+r\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$
$+p\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial\beta^3}+r\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}+s\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}$
$\frac{\frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial\alpha^2}\frac{\partial q}{\partial\beta^2}-\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}\frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial\beta^2}}{\frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial\alpha^2}\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}-\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}}=a$
$\frac{\frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}-\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}\frac{\partial p}{\partial\alpha}}{\frac{\partial p}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial q}{\partial\beta}-\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}}=a$
$\frac{\partial\log[?]\ldots}{\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}-\frac{\partial p}{\partial\alpha}}=w$
